A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SSDD work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated theory and renumbered qualitative figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original SSDD reconstruction and DiT generation experiments on ImageNet, with architectural ablations, sampling analyses and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 reports original SSDD experiments, including revised ImageNet results, COCO generalization, additional encoder comparisons and new distillation controls.

M1.justification: Appendix D adds an input linear projection to adapt SSDD conditioning to DC-AE latents at f32c32 and f64c128. The central architecture, flow-matching/LPIPS/REPA objectives, shared-encoder procedure and teacher-student distillation remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates image reconstruction and generation on ImageNet. v2 adds reconstruction on COCO-2017 using ImageNet-trained models (Table 5), introducing a substantial cross-dataset generalization test while retaining the original ImageNet tasks.

E2.justification: v2 adds the Consistency decoder to Tables 1–2, continuous FlowMo to Table 1, native DC-AE decoders to Table S3, and an evaluated MeanFlow alternative in Appendix D. Table S3 removes the SD-VAE-XL comparator. These substantially broaden the evaluated alternatives beyond the retained baseline set.

E3.justification: New protocols include COCO evaluation on 5,000 images at 256 and 512 resolution and ImageNet evaluation at 1024 using models optimized at 256. Table S3 changes from eight-step SSDD comparisons to distilled models, expands encoder configurations and removes PSNR/SSIM reporting. H-model results disappear while XL appears throughout the main comparisons. The main training budgets remain documented as before; numerical revisions alone do not establish changed training procedures.

E4.justification: Table S5 adds controls testing adversarial loss on the distilled decoder and L2-only distillation. Appendix D additionally tests direct MeanFlow training, while Table 5 examines cross-dataset robustness. Frozen-encoder and resolution analyses are expanded, and new Figure S5 provides a perceptual-versus-pixel-fidelity case study. These extend the existing sequential ablation and sampling analyses substantially.

E5.justification: Neither version reports benchmark confidence intervals, repeated-training seed counts or formal significance tests. Both retain per-pixel standard deviations over 64 decodings in the diversity visualization, renumbered from Figure S7 to S8. The signed differences in ablation tables are result deltas, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Reported results change extensively. In Table 1, f8c4 SSDD-S rFID changes from 0.50 to 0.46 and DiTo-XL-LPIPS from 0.78 to 1.06. Table 3 reverses SSDD-S versus KL-VAE under CFG: 7.33 versus 7.53 becomes 8.02 versus 7.63. Table S2 also reverses the direction of several distillation effects. New COCO, 1024-resolution, DC-AE and control results are added; changed-setting Table S3 entries cannot be treated as direct performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 corrects the constant-compression relation from f^2*c=16 to f^2/c=16. Otherwise the theoretical arguments are retained: the LPIPS gradient derivation moves from Appendix A.2 to Section 3.3, and the distortion-distribution supporting claims remain in Appendix A. This is a limited mathematical correction, not a new theoretical contribution.

C1.justification: The architecture, GAN-free training and efficient single-step decoding remain the central contributions. v2 qualifies the novelty claim as the first GAN-free single-step decoder to reach state-of-the-art continuous tokenization, adds an explicit no-divergence claim, and strengthens the conclusion's decoding-speed comparison against epsilon-VAE-H from approximately 3x to 10x.

C2.justification: Appendix D adds explanations for retaining perceptual loss, avoiding adversarial distillation and preferring train-then-distill over MeanFlow. It distinguishes quality-critical components from standard training and pipeline choices. Appendix C revises where distillation benefits generation, and Appendix E explicitly acknowledges realistic details differing from the original. These refine the existing perception-distortion interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 documents the DC-AE conditioning projection and GAN-weight selection, and labels externally sourced Table 1 results more explicitly. It removes the reproducibility statement promising supplementary training code and future weight release, while retaining the repository link and most implementation settings. H200 throughput-measurement details move from Appendix B to Section 4.1; they are not newly disclosed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Betker et al. for the Consistency decoder, Geng et al. for MeanFlow, and Lin et al. for COCO, with new positioning against direct single-step training. The narrower novelty wording also qualifies its relationship to prior decoders. The broader literature framing is retained; publication updates and added reference URLs do not constitute new cited works.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites portions of the introduction, presents the reconstruction criteria as a numbered list, expands explanatory passages and captions, and moves the LPIPS derivation into Section 3.3. The reproducibility section is removed. The overall main-section and appendix organization remains recognizable, with most existing prose retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5 and S5 and a new qualitative Figure S5, expands Table 2 with 1024-resolution columns, and substantially restructures Table S3. Figures S1–S4 are rearranged into stacked panels, with revised plotted content and legends where applicable. The earlier qualitative Figures S5–S7 are retained as S6–S8 rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: COCO transfer results, broader decoder comparisons and the GAN/L2-only controls strengthen evidence for generalization and the training choices beyond v1. The improvement is limited by unreconciled result revisions and stale claims: v2 still says SSDD-S beats all generation baselines despite Table 3 reporting CFG gFID 8.02 versus KL-VAE's 7.63, and prose still discusses removed H-model results. The added validation supports a modest net quality gain rather than a major improvement.
